goal: Lets operators pin BIP152 high-bandwidth compact-block announcements to specific -addnode peers.
Useful for known low-latency or multi-location topologies, independent of automatic peer selection.

result.summary: This PR adds an opt-in `=bip152-hb` suffix to `-addnode` values, letting operators request persistent BIP152 high-bandwidth compact-block announcements from specific outbound added-node peers, independent of and additional to the node's automatic 3-peer high-bandwidth selection. It refactors AddedNodeParams to carry per-node settings through CConnman, matches durable outbound peers to configured endpoints without DNS lookups, reapplies the policy on reconnect, and rejects the suffix when combined with -blocksonly. Tests cover unit-level endpoint matching and functional peer behavior across reconnects.
result.problem: Automatic BIP152 high-bandwidth selection cannot account for operator-known topology, such as a stable low-latency peering link or nodes run in multiple locations that should always announce compact blocks immediately, including after reconnects.

result.card: This PR adds an opt-in `-addnode=<host>=bip152-hb` suffix so operators can pin BIP152 high-bandwidth compact-block announcements to specific outbound added-node peers, persisting across reconnects and stacking additively on top of the existing automatic 3-peer selection. It solves a narrow but real operator pain point: no existing way to guarantee immediate, consistent high-bandwidth relay for a known-good link such as a stable low-latency peer or a node run across multiple locations. The only reviewer, jeanpablojp, gave a concept ACK with reasoning ('explicit operator choice ... disclosed upfront') and the one inline nit (rename the release-notes file) was fixed in the latest push, leaving the PR Ready with Strong agreement and no open concerns. It has no dependencies and does not block other work, though the author notes BIP152 itself could later be updated to reflect this pattern. Impact is confined to p2p (P3, an opt-in niche feature) and docs (P4, a standard release note).
